heading: What the week could look like
review: These cases illustrate the design. A plan to follow will be available after professional review.
uncovered: The example catalogue does not cover this combination of answers.
strengthWeek: In the bench strength case, both sessions start with the chosen lift. Leg and back work follow the bench press.
muscleWeek: In the chest-focused case, both sessions repeat the press. The person in this example also wants to train their triceps and includes a cable exercise.
entryWeek: In the introductory or returning case, both sessions repeat the same movements for practice. The person keeps their usual walks.
generalWeek: The general fitness case combines familiar movements and usual walks. The person checks whether both activities fit the available time.
aerobicWeek: In the aerobic case, the duration and effort of the usual walks take priority. Familiar strength work fits around them.
aerobicEntryWeek: In the introductory aerobic case, familiar walks take priority while the person learns the strength movements.
strengthSetup: This case assumes familiarity with a trap bar, an adjustable bench and access to both stations. Estimates include preparation, transitions and rests.
muscleSetup: This case assumes an adjustable bench and a familiar cable station. Estimates include preparation, transitions and rests.
mixedSetup: This case assumes two usual 10-minute walks, a chest press machine, a bench, dumbbells and access to the floor. The estimates include walking. The questionnaire does not check every detail.
row: Chest-supported dumbbell row on an incline bench
walk: The same time slot includes 10 minutes of habitual walking.
focus: The documented week covers a different priority from the one you chose.
startingPoint: The available case assumes a different starting point.
days: The example schedule needs two available days.
duration: At least one session exceeds your available time.
equipment: The example uses equipment you have not listed.
preference: The week includes an exercise you prefer to avoid.
spacing: The example assumes a free day between sessions.
familiarity: The case assumes familiarity with movements you have not selected.
walking: The case includes habitual walks. Your answers do not establish recent aerobic activity.
incomplete: Complete answers are needed to compare the week.
overBudget: The estimate exceeds your available {minutes} minutes.
omitCable: Leave out the last cable set for this session
shortSummary: You recorded seven of eight sets and left out the final cable set.
savedProgress: Sets recorded in this session: {count} of {total}
